title: Bandwidth
description: Scheduled bandwidth tests from bandwidth-exporter. Results are cached: each value is the most recent test, not a live rate.

panels.title: Download
panels.description: Most recent successful download, measured at the receiver, warm-up excluded.

panels.title: Upload
panels.description: Most recent successful upload, counted from the bytes the far end acknowledged.

panels.title: Idle latency
panels.description: Median TCP handshake time to the target before the load.

panels.title: Latency under download
panels.description: Median handshake time while the download ran. Far above idle latency means bufferbloat.

panels.title: Since last success
panels.description: Time since the most recent successful test finished.

panels.title: Last attempt
panels.description: Whether the most recent attempt succeeded.

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Each step is one test. The value holds until the next successful test; failed runs never show up as zero.

panels.title: Latency
panels.description: Round-trip time idle and under load. The gap between them is working latency (bufferbloat).

panels.title: Jitter
panels.description: Mean absolute difference between consecutive idle round-trip times.

panels.title: Runs per day
panels.description: Attempts, failures and deliberately skipped runs over the trailing day. Skips (budget, rate limiting) are the exporter choosing not to measure.

panels.title: Data moved by tests
panels.description: Every byte the tests moved, warm-up and probes included, against the configured budget.

panels.title: Configured tests
panels.description: Context recorded with each test's most recent run, and its schedule.

targets.expr: max by (test, peer, backend, target, server, streams, cca, ip_family, network_mode, method, tool_version) (bandwidth_test_info{cluster=~"$cluster", test=~"$test"})

panels.title: Pairs: latest results
panels.description: One row per tester (node) and peer. Throughput in bit/s from the most recent successful test of each pair.

targets.expr: 8 * max by (node, zone, test, peer, peer_zone) (bandwidth_download_bytes_per_second{cluster=~"$cluster", test=~"$test", kind="east_west"})
8 * max by (node, zone, test, peer, peer_zone) (bandwidth_upload_bytes_per_second{cluster=~"$cluster", test=~"$test", kind="east_west"})
max by (node, zone, test, peer, peer_zone) (bandwidth_idle_latency_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", test=~"$test", kind="east_west"})
1000 * max by (node, zone, test, peer, peer_zone) (bandwidth_last_success_timestamp_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", test=~"$test", kind="east_west"} > 0)

panels.title: East/west download by pair
panels.description: Peer to tester. Each step is one test of that pair.

panels.title: Responder: refused requests per day
panels.description: Slots granted to peers, and refusals by reason. auth or replay mean someone without the peer key is knocking; busy and business_hours are the design working.

panels.title: Zone to zone: latest results
panels.description: East/west pairs grouped by the tester's zone and the peer's (the exporter's `zones` setting). The slowest pair and the highest idle latency between two zones, so one bad path is not averaged away.

targets.expr: 8 * min by (zone, peer_zone) (bandwidth_download_bytes_per_second{cluster=~"$cluster", test=~"$test", kind="east_west", zone!="", peer_zone!=""})
8 * min by (zone, peer_zone) (bandwidth_upload_bytes_per_second{cluster=~"$cluster", test=~"$test", kind="east_west", zone!="", peer_zone!=""})
max by (zone, peer_zone) (bandwidth_idle_latency_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", test=~"$test", kind="east_west", zone!="", peer_zone!=""})
count by (zone, peer_zone) (bandwidth_download_bytes_per_second{cluster=~"$cluster", test=~"$test", kind="east_west", zone!="", peer_zone!=""})

panels.title: Zone to zone download
panels.description: The slowest pair between each two zones, over time.

targets.expr: 8 * min by (zone, peer_zone) (bandwidth_download_bytes_per_second{cluster=~"$cluster", test=~"$test", kind="east_west", zone!="", peer_zone!=""})

panels.title: Zone to zone idle latency
panels.description: TCP connect time before each test, the highest pair between each two zones.

targets.expr: max by (zone, peer_zone) (bandwidth_idle_latency_seconds{cluster=~"$cluster", test=~"$test", kind="east_west", zone!="", peer_zone!=""})

panels.title: Test running
panels.description: 1 while the single test worker is busy.

panels.title: Queued runs
panels.description: Runs waiting for the worker. Tests never overlap.

panels.title: Last run CPU-bound
panels.description: Yes means CPU, not the network, may have limited the last result.

panels.title: CPU quota
panels.description: The container's CFS quota in cores. Unlimited is what the chart sets, on purpose.
